newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines approves early U.S. sugar shipment.
newsitem.headline: Philippines approves early U.S. sugar shipment.

text.p: The Philippines had approved the early shipment of locally grown sugar to the United States to fulfill its sugar quota for crop year 1996-1997, Agriculture officials said on Friday.

Agriculture officials told reporters the department had approved the export of around 75,000 tonnes of sugar to the United States between October and December this year, and another 75,000 tonnes between January and March 1997.

The Philippines, one of the beneficiaries of a programme under which developing nations export sugar to the United States at premium prices, is expected to get a 285,000-tonne sugar quota from the United States in crop year 1996-1997 ending August.
The United States granted an export quota of 229,393 tonnes to the Philippines for crop year 1995-1996.
Philippine sugar millers and planters said they expected local sugar production to increase to between 1.9 to 2.0 million tonnes in the next crop year.
Production for crop year 1995-1996 was expected to hit 1.78 million tonnes.

"Sugar production for the new crop year which starts on September 1 is expected to rise (on expectations) of better weather conditions and the even distribution of rainfall," said Greg Saguinsin, executive vice president of the Confederation of Sugar Producers Association.

Philippine millers and planters say they expected domestic sugar surplus in 1995-96 to rise to 494,470 tonnes from the earlier estimate of 350,000 tonnes in the last crop year due to heavy importation since September 1995 .
